cells.tense: You're in the stretch where the meeting is real and chosen, and you're not lost in it — the two streams ran together because you picked the run.
cells.ask: Spend one evening together with nothing decided and nothing to report afterward, then say out loud to yourself what direction it pointed. It hands you the pull you can already feel, named.
cells.core:
A kitchen where two people cook without an audience is what this looks like when it's working: no performance, both of you more honest by the end than at the start, and the honest part isn't a cost. You're becoming more of what you are inside this, not less.

What's already flowing is direction. Enough meetings between the two of you have stacked into a pull, and defending it is the natural next move — gathered, certain, aimed at what the two of you actually yield. You don't need more proof before you take it. One clear step today is enough, and taking it tells you where the pull was real.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this stream and it's pointed somewhere — take one step today.
cells.verb: choose one stream to flow with and let the two make a single direction; go meet when moving alone fails
cells.place: showing what you actually are without covering it over; letting what's inherent ride out to where it can be seen

cells.tense: You're already living inside a merged outcome that hasn't happened — writing the two of you into a future you can't sign for, and bracing for it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's past the still-forming stage and finish it — those dishes, that folder, the last bit of it. Notice it's done. It gives back the feel of something complete.
cells.core:
The connection is real; the meeting is one thing, and the merger you keep rehearsing is another. What's run ahead of the calendar is the arranging — where you'll live, how it'll go, what they'll do next — while the two of you are still here, still forming. That's not wrong, it just keeps you busy with a room nobody's standing in.

What's underneath is care. Protecting something because it matters is good tending, and it gets to stay. The opening is to tend what's here instead of what's imagined, tending it root by root out of what you two actually build on a Tuesday — and a thing finished today is the proof that you can leave something alone once it's whole.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing a future instead of showing up for the one forming.

cells.tense: You're still standing where a choice to merge was once made — not in the meeting and not in the merge, off to the side of both, nearer to sure of not being received than to trying.
cells.ask: Ask one person one real question — where they actually are in one thing that matters — and stay for the whole answer without planning your reply. It gives the meeting a place to land.
cells.core:
The direction you set is still visible from where you stand, and you can still see who it was for. A table where people put their cards down without checking the door first is what this looks like when it's alive — the talk going both ways, the answers arriving unfiltered.

The moving stopped, not the want. Questioning whether you still want the merge is the first act of it, not a delay on someone else's clock. Asking a real question and leaving room for the answer is the only proof available today that the other end is still there — and the answer, whatever it is, is more useful to you than the waiting has been.
cells.sheetLine: You set the direction and stopped stepping — ask something real and let the answer do the rest.
cells.verb: choose one stream to flow with and let the two make a single direction; go meet when moving alone fails
cells.place: showing what you actually are without covering it over; letting what's inherent ride out to where it can be seen

cells.tense: The merging that shapes how you live is already running — who you keep close, what direction you move in — and you describe it as something that happens to you.
cells.ask: Say one sentence plainly to someone inside this: this connection shapes what we do, and it's being picked, not drifted into. It gives the pick a place to stand next to.
cells.core:
Merging into something lasting is a choice, and it's being made in who you turn toward, whose direction you move with, which connections hold. A flat kept for two people is still a flat; the deciding shows up in how it's kept, not in a speech about it. None of it may register as deciding.

Practice wants to be tended without a written contract. The move is to say one thing that's already true out loud — not a declaration, just putting a name on a decision that's been operating without one. Naming it once makes the next move in that direction easier to find, and easier to mean.
cells.sheetLine: This connection is already a choice — put your name on it once.

attempts.check: The unsupported move is any inner motive the record doesn't carry — that they're merging to be taken care of, or that merging ever went badly in a way that told them something. The reader could rightly say it's the other stream, not them, that won't meet, or that nothing in their life feels like pre-work at all. The asks survive that: each one is a single outward act — show the untidy thing, make a dated move, ask a real question — that teaches something even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me most is the third status's framing of not being received; I've written it forward instead of dressing it as a wound the record doesn't have.

attempts.check: The unsupported move in this draft is motive — that merging is being done to be taken care of, or that a past meeting 'wasn't received' in a way that taught a lesson. The record says nothing about who ended it, how long it has run, or what they concluded; a reader could rightly answer that the other person is the one withholding, and the card would still hold. The asks survive that, because each is one visible act — an evening with no verdict, a question answered fully, a sentence said out loud — that teaches something either way. The sentence serving me most is the third one's framing of standing off to the side of a choice already made; it leans toward a wound the record does not establish, so it becomes a location rather than a story.
